decision: harden the accepted v1 contracts in risk order
why: process containment and session shutdown can lose control of workloads, so they come before policy and diagnostics

decision: launch every workload suspended with an explicit inherited-handle list, assign it to the Job Object, then resume
why: no workload instruction may run before containment

decision: replace the nested ending-event name with one flat Global name
why: Windows reserves backslashes in kernel object names after the namespace prefix
result: invalid ADR detail corrected before implementation

decision: make SCM session and preshutdown notifications signal one per-session event watched by controller and supervisors
why: logout must stop workloads even when controller RPC is gone
result: controller, supervisor, and workload stopped with durable stopped history

decision: persist typed checkpoints and observations, commit cursor before ACK, replace lost supervisors without duplicating executions
why: controller and supervisor crashes must not lose terminal facts or silently rerun jobs
result: service survived supervisor and controller replacement in one execution; attempt result was prevented from masquerading as terminal result

decision: separate process-definition drift from journal-acknowledged policy delivery
why: process changes must not mutate a live execution while policy changes should apply without restart
result: policy applied to the same supervisor and process drift set restart_required without replacing the execution

decision: launch controllers from validated immutable selections and preserve current or execution-pinned versions during GC
why: stable bin copies cannot safely preserve an old supervisor runtime format across controller upgrades
result: stable bin contains only the CLI; pinned old build survived GC and was removed after its pin disappeared

decision: persist SID plus AuthenticationId and controller process identity in a volatile registry mapping
why: a host service restart must adopt the exact live controller without carrying a manager session into a later logon
result: disconnect remains live; PID reuse, session mismatch, and logon mismatch force a fresh controller

decision: claim each enabled job once per host-issued manager session in SQLite
why: controller recovery in one logon must not duplicate a one-shot execution
result: enabled services resume normally and enabled jobs are at-most-once per manager session

decision: centralize non-blocking JSONL segmentation and retention in one shared module
why: lifecycle control must never block on operator diagnostics and every process needs bounded storage
result: controller emitted complete start, reload, and stop records and finalized its segment on shutdown

decision: close active rows from older manager sessions instead of recovering them
why: recovery is valid across controller replacement in one logon, never across logout or reboot
result: old jobs become outcome-unknown, old services become stopped, and enabled triggers own any new execution

decision: key ending markers by Windows session plus AuthenticationId and preserve a live controller during same-SID conflicts
why: Windows can reuse numeric session IDs and v1 must not duplicate or accidentally stop controllers
result: new logons cannot inherit stale ending markers; conflicts are explicit without starting a second controller

decision: require protocol, formatting, lint, test, release, packaging, and diff checks before commit
why: the hardening crosses process, persistence, transport, and installer boundaries
evidence: buf lint/build; cargo fmt/clippy/test/build --release; PACKAGE_SMOKE_OK; git diff --check
